definition: subject to sudden or unpredictable mood changes
memoryTip: Mercury races across the sky—mercurial people change moods just as fast.
correctPassage: Her mercurial moods made long-term planning with her difficult.
wrongPassages: The bridge was mercurial, standing for centuries without a single repair.
He kept a mercurial schedule that never varied by even a minute.
The committee wanted mercurial rules so nothing would ever need updating.

memoryTip: Obey-sequious: so eager to please it turns into fawning.
correctPassage: Obsequious assistants hovered, waiting for the slightest request.
wrongPassages: The general's obsequious refusal to follow orders cost the unit the battle.
Her obsequious critique demolished every assumption the panel cherished.
He was so obsequious that he never spoke to anyone above his own rank.

definition: done secretly, especially because it would not be approved
memoryTip: Surreptitious sneak—on the sly because it wouldn't be allowed.
correctPassage: A surreptitious glance at his notes did not go unnoticed.
wrongPassages: The mayor made a surreptitious announcement on live television to the whole city.
Their surreptitious wedding was livestreamed with open invitations for all.
She left a surreptitious notice taped to the office door where everyone could see it.

definition: having knowledge of events before they take place
memoryTip: Pre-science: knows what will happen before it does.
correctPassage: Her prescient warning about housing risk was ignored until too late.
wrongPassages: His prescient summary only restated what everyone already knew from yesterday's news.
The prescient report carefully avoided any claim about what might happen next.
She was praised as prescient for documenting events only after they had finished.

definition: attacking or rejecting cherished beliefs or institutions
correctPassage: An iconoclastic critic challenged nearly every received opinion in the field.
wrongPassages: The museum's iconoclastic exhibit carefully preserved every traditional display.
Her iconoclastic loyalty to the founding charter never wavered for decades.
The board praised his iconoclastic refusal to question any established policy.
